Why this matters

Data centers are becoming strategic infrastructure.

Advanced computing depends on more than servers and chips. Data-center growth also requires large, reliable power supplies; transmission and utility coordination; access to land and water; workable permitting and policy environments; and durable relationships with host communities.

This platform brings those systems into a common geographic frame. It helps researchers and decision-makers identify concentrations, compare development contexts, test spatial relationships, and find places that warrant deeper investigation.

The current release focuses on the United States. It establishes the analytical foundation for a broader comparative assessment of U.S. and People’s Republic of China data-center ecosystems, dependencies, and strategic vulnerabilities.

Research design

Eight layers, one auditable evidence base

The platform distinguishes reported facts, derived measures, spatial context, and unresolved fields. Missing information remains visible rather than being converted to zero or “no.”

01

Facility inventory

Locations, project status, reported capacity, power source, cooling, ownership, and timing.

02

Power supply

EPA eGRID generation, fuel mix, capacity, output, emissions, and regional grid geography.

03

Grid geography

Candidate utility territories, eGRID subregions, balancing-area context, and utility characteristics.

04

Infrastructure pressure

Transmission and substation proximity, nearby generation, interconnection queues, and utility-relative scale.

05

Water and hazards

Water scarcity, historical withdrawals, drought, flood, heat, wildfire, and overall physical risk.

06

Land and development

Reported acreage, county facility concentration, and employment and payroll context.

07

Legislation and policy

State incentives, moratorium records, bill status, and 22 non-exclusive policy topics.

08

Local response

Direct facility evidence, county tracker context, local-government actions, and evidence status.

How to interpret the evidence

Context supports inquiry. It does not replace verification.

Proximity is contextual

A nearby line, substation, generator, or water source does not establish a physical connection, available capacity, or a service agreement.

Coverage varies

Capacity, power-source, cooling, utility, and opposition fields depend on public reporting. “Unknown” is retained as a substantive category.

Relationships are descriptive

Correlations, spatial clusters, policy exposure, and tracker matches identify patterns for follow-up; they do not establish causal effects.

A living research platform

Built for transparent iteration

Each layer retains source information, measurement rules, match quality, and interpretation limits. The platform will evolve as facility records change, additional evidence becomes available, and the comparative research expands.
